title: Sign of the Magic Number
src: Media.net OA, college not given (PDF write-up), problem 1.
body:
You are given a permutation A of 1..N. For each position i, its magic number is

(smaller values to its left × smaller values to its right) − (larger values to its left × larger values to its right).

Return an array whose i-th entry is 1 if the magic number at i is ≥ 0, and −1 if it is negative.

Function to complete

Complete magicSigns(A). It returns 1 or -1 for every position.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
cons: 1 ≤ N ≤ 6 × 10<sup>4</sup> (reported: 10<sup>5</sup>; lowered so the output fits the runner's 200 KB limit)

wrong.why: counts with two nested loops, O(N²) (too slow)
treats a magic number of exactly 0 as negative
wrong.ref:
class Solution:
    def magicSigns(self, A):
        n = len(A); bit = [0] * (n + 1); res = []
        for i, v in enumerate(A):
            s, k = 0, v - 1
            while k > 0: s += bit[k]; k -= k & -k
            sr = v - 1 - s; ll = i - s; lr = n - 1 - i - sr
            res.append(1 if s * sr - ll * lr > 0 else -1)
            k = v
            while k <= n: bit[k] += 1; k += k & -k
        return res

samples.ex: For 1 (index 2): 0 smaller anywhere, 2 larger on each side, so 0 − 4 < 0 → −1. For 4 (index 3): 2·1 − 1·0 = 2 → 1.
